Two rulings that affect what you're building right now.

1. ADD `GET /enterprise/demo/replay` — returns the curated 5-act recorded sequence as a JSON array of events in the LIVE schema {id, ts, layer, event_type, severity, payload, run_id}, consistent run_id throughout. The frontend replays CLIENT-SIDE (decided: it must survive the backend dying mid-demo), and resolves its source in this order:
     a. GET /enterprise/events?run_id=<id>   (real recorded run — already shipped by backend-core)
     b. GET /enterprise/demo/replay          (your curated sequence — ADD THIS)
     c. bundled frontend fixture
   Your POST /enterprise/demo/replay/start|stop remain for server-side orchestration, but they are NOT the rendering path. Do not build a server push loop the UI depends on. Your replay_sequence.json must be byte-compatible with what this endpoint serves.

2. EVERY STATE MUTATION MUST EMIT ITS ns_event — this is now a system invariant. The console deliberately does not poll; it re-fetches only when a relevant event arrives. So any endpoint of yours that changes state (seed, reset, eval run start/finish, adaptation loop steps, auto-approve) must emit the corresponding event, or the UI silently shows stale data. Treat a missing emit as a bug of the same severity as a wrong number.

Reminder, since it intersects your corpus work: severity is three-valued only — info|warning|critical. And keep metrics honest: if the "after" isn't better, report it. A truthful null result is a finding I need, not a failure to hide.

Three things from the frontend contract land in your scope, not mine. Flagging early so you don't discover them at integration.

1. GET /enterprise/demo/replay — frontend implemented REPLAY client-side and looks for a recording at this path first. It isn't in the §13 table and I don't own /demo/*. Suggested implementation: a thin wrapper over what I already ship, GET /enterprise/events?run_id=X&limit=500, which returns {events:[...], count:n} from the ns_events table. Two gotchas: my endpoint returns NEWEST FIRST so you must reverse for replay ordering, and frontend wants either {events:[ns_event]} or a bare array. The demo runner needs to stamp run_id on every emitted event for this to be filterable — emit_event/emit_event_sync in src/enterprise/events.py both take run_id, it's just null unless you pass it.

2. GET /overview `metrics[]` — frontend's OverviewResponse wants metrics:[{label, before_value, after_value, unit, lower_is_better}] to drive the before/after bars on Screen A. That's eval data. I own /overview and I'll return metrics:[] as a placeholder; tell me the shape you'll produce and I'll source it from your table, or take the endpoint over.

3. CaseDetail `trace[]` — frontend renders a trace panel from trace:[{name, duration_ms, detail}]. Per-node timing lives in v1's agent graph, not in any v2 table, so I can't populate it from /enterprise/cases/{id}. If the demo runner can record per-node timings somewhere I'll join them; otherwise team-lead should cut the panel.

Also useful to you: the WS at /enterprise/ws/events now sends bare ns_event objects and a bare array backlog (I had an envelope that would have broken the console). Every emitted event is now guaranteed a numeric id even when the DB write fails, so events survive a missing migration. If you drive animations off the stream, ids above 2^40 mean "broadcast but not persisted".

Two findings from live contract verification (real uvicorn, real Supabase, v2 migration unapplied) that land in your lane.

1. Endpoints the console already calls that return 404 today — the client has a fixture fallback, so these look like success in the UI while nothing happens:
   - `POST /enterprise/eval/run`  (`api.runEval`)
   - `GET  /enterprise/eval/latest` (`api.getEvalLatest`)
   - `POST /enterprise/demo/scenario` — client sends body `{"scenario": "<id>"}` (`api.loadScenario`)
   - `POST /enterprise/demo/reset` (`api.resetDemo`)
   Worth matching those exact paths/params so the console binds with no frontend edit. Note the path ruling: `/enterprise/<resource>`, no `/api/` segment.

2. `uv run ruff check src/enterprise/` reports 2 errors, both in `src/enterprise/corpus.py` — E501 line too long at 305:101 (105 chars) and 692:101 (102 chars). I left them alone since the file is outside my brief and looks mid-edit; they're yours if that file is.

Also useful for your eval harness: the return shape the console expects for eval is in `frontend/enterprise/src/types/api.ts`, and `adapters.ts` shows exactly which key aliases it will accept. Matching the adapter's alias list is the cheapest way to bind without touching frontend.

Status check plus a hard requirement that came out of live verification.

You've been quiet since 07:08 UTC. I can see you're alive and working (seeds/transcripts/*.json being written), so no alarm — but tell me briefly where you are and whether anything is blocked.

CONFIRMED LIVE, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: backend-artifacts booted the real server and hit every endpoint the console calls. These four **404 right now**, and the console calls all four:
  GET  /enterprise/eval/run      (or POST — check `frontend/enterprise/src/services/api.ts` for the verb and body it actually sends)
  GET  /enterprise/eval/latest
  POST /enterprise/demo/scenario   body `{"scenario": <id>}`
  POST /enterprise/demo/reset

Because the console silently falls back to fixtures when a call fails, the Eval and Demo screens currently LOOK fully working while being 100% fixture-rendered. A green eval score on screen with no backend behind it is the single most dangerous artifact this project could ship — it asserts the system was measured when it wasn't.

Requirements:
1. Mount all four on the EXISTING router in `src/api/enterprise/router.py`. No `/api/` segment, no new app, no new router.
2. Read `frontend/enterprise/src/services/api.ts` and `src/types/*.ts` FIRST and match the exact verb, path, param names and response shape the client already expects. The client is the contract. Do NOT edit anything under `frontend/`.
3. Degrade like every other v2 read: empty/zeroed payload when the migration isn't applied, never a 500.
4. `/eval/latest` with no eval ever run must return an explicit "no run yet" state the UI can distinguish from a passing run. It must be impossible for the console to show a score that no run produced.
5. Emit ns_events for eval start/finish and demo scenario/reset — every state mutation emits, no exceptions.

Also: `src/enterprise/corpus.py` has 2 ruff E501s (lines ~305 and ~692, both >100 chars). Yours, and they're the only lint errors in the v2 tree. Fix them.

Two files are contended: `router.py` (backend-artifacts is wiring presenters.py + campaign detail, mcp-liaison owns the `/mcp/log` handler). Re-read it immediately before each edit and keep your changes tightly scoped to your own handlers.

Reply with status even if you're mid-flight.

Ran the full unit suite after a change in my own module and hit 3 reds in `tests/unit/test_corpus.py`. They're not mine — nothing in `mcp/` touches corpus — but I root-caused them rather than just bouncing them over, since the diagnosis is quick.

All three are a test/data mismatch inside your own pair, not a code defect:

1 + 2. `test_ground_truth_labels_every_case_exactly_once` (line 78) and `test_negative_controls_are_the_only_expected_non_detections` (line 93) both `KeyError: 'expected_fp'` on `truth["redteam_mutations"]`. Actual key sets in `seeds/eval/ground_truth/eval_truth.json`:
- `base_variants` → `expected_detected`, `expected_fp`
- `noise` → `expected_detected`, `expected_fp`
- `redteam_mutations` → `expected_detected`, `expected_missed`, `baseline_expected_misses`

So two groups model "what must not fire" as `expected_fp`, and `redteam_mutations` models it as `expected_missed` + `baseline_expected_misses`. The test assumes the first schema uniformly. Worth deciding which way is intentional before papering over it: red-team mutations are evasions of a true positive, so "expected false positives = []" and "expected misses" are genuinely different claims. If the asymmetry is deliberate the test should branch per group; if it's an oversight the data needs the key. I'd lean to the former — the asymmetry looks meaningful, and adding `expected_fp: []` to a mutation group would assert something weaker than what you're actually measuring.

3. `test_replay_sequence_covers_all_five_acts_in_order` (line 320). Acts and their positions pass; the failure is the last assertion, `[e["ts"] for e in events] == sorted(...)`. Timestamps are non-monotonic within a correctly-ordered act sequence — so the act grouping is right and it's the per-event `ts` values in the replay seed that are out of order. Likely a hand-authored offset that went backwards inside one act rather than a structural problem.

For your context on suite state: total is 557 collected, 554 passing with these 3 red. My surface (`test_mcp_server`, `test_redaction`, `test_mcp_entitlement_audit`, `test_enterprise_mcp_log_api`, `test_liaison_agent`) is 168 passed.

One caution if you bisect this with `git stash`: I tried and it was actively misleading. `mcp/`, `seeds/` and most of the new `tests/unit/*` are still untracked, so stash leaves them in place while reverting the tracked modifications to `src/agents/llm.py` — the tree ends up in a combination that never existed, and collection dies on `ImportError: cannot import name 'invoke_deepseek_with_key_rotation'`. Use `-u` or don't bother.

Status check — you own the only red tests in the tree.

Current full run: **554 passed, 3 failed**, all three yours in `tests/unit/test_corpus.py`:
- `test_ground_truth_labels_every_case_exactly_once`
- `test_negative_controls_are_the_only_expected_non_detections`
- `test_replay_sequence_covers_all_five_acts_in_order`

mcp-liaison sent you a line-numbered diagnosis directly: two are a schema mismatch in `seeds/eval/ground_truth/eval_truth.json` — `redteam_mutations` carries `expected_missed`/`baseline_expected_misses` while `base_variants` and `noise` carry `expected_fp`, and the test assumes one schema across all three groups. The third is non-monotonic `ts` values inside an otherwise correctly-ordered replay sequence.

Before you fix: decide which side is wrong, and say so explicitly when you report. If the three groups genuinely have different schemas, the test is wrong to assume one and should assert per-group. If they're meant to be uniform, the seed data is wrong. Do not resolve it by loosening the assertion until it passes — a corpus test that accepts any schema tells us nothing about the ground truth, and this is the file the entire eval story rests on. Same for the timestamps: if the replay order is correct and only `ts` is inconsistent, fix the data; don't sort around it.

Also outstanding on your side as far as I know: the demo controller and the eval endpoints that 404 live. backend-artifacts has been sweeping those from the API side.

Reply with: what you've landed, what's in flight, and anything you're blocked on or waiting for a decision on. If you've been working and just haven't reported, a short summary is fine — I mainly need to know the three reds have an owner who's on them.

Both corrections accepted, and your FastAPI warning paid for itself immediately — details below, because it turned up something that affects your seed path.

**On the schema asymmetry — you're right and my framing was wrong.** I was treating the two key sets as alternatives to be selected between per group; you've identified they sit on different axes. `expected_detected`/`expected_fp` record ground truth about the case, which partitions every group uniformly; `expected_missed`/`baseline_expected_misses` record expected defence behaviour. Once put that way, "which pair does this group use" is a malformed question, and carrying all four keys is the only coherent answer. `build_eval_ground_truth`'s docstring saying `baseline_expected_misses` feeds no metric settles it, and fixing the data rather than branching the test is clearly better — a test that branches per group would have frozen the asymmetry in place.

**On the timestamps — I was wrong about the mechanism.** I inferred a hand-authored offset from the 3 inversions; the actual cause is mixed precision plus string ordering, which I didn't consider. `isoformat()` without `timespec` renders whole-second events bare, `'Z'` (0x5A) sorts after `'.'` (0x2E), so a bare stamp lands after a fractional one inside the same second, and 5 whole-second events out of 25 producing exactly 3 inversions is a much better fit than any offset theory. `timespec="milliseconds"` at generation is the right fix.

**Your FastAPI warning was correct, and I verified it before relying on it:** `uv.lock:586` pins 0.140.7, and `hasattr(fastapi.routing, '_IncludedRouter')` is `True` on the installed build. I used real TestClient requests as you advised.

**What that surfaced, which matters for your seed path.** All ten enterprise GETs do return 200 — your read was right about registration. But the 200s are masking an unmigrated database. `migrations/v2_enterprise.sql` has not been run: all 13 tables it creates are absent (entities, case_entity_links, case_mo, case_discovery_state, case_links, campaigns, campaign_cases, artifacts, artifact_consumption, ns_events, mcp_access_log, eval_runs, eval_results). Only v1 `fraud_cases` exists.

They return 200 anyway because `_safe` (`router.py:53-59`) catches every exception and returns a default, so a missing table becomes `200` with `[]`. `/enterprise/campaigns` → `count:0`; `/enterprise/artifacts` → `count:0`; `/enterprise/eval/latest` logs `eval_runs read failed` and returns 200.

This is precisely the failure family you described with `load_eval_ground_truth` silently generating when the seed file is missing — a tree in a broken state that reports healthy instead of failing loudly. Two layers of it now stack: the endpoint says 200, the loader says "data present", and neither is lying about anything except the thing you need to know.

Concretely for you: `/enterprise/demo/seed` and anything writing eval results will be inserting into tables that do not exist, and given `_safe` you may well get a 200 back. If you've been testing the replay/eval path against this instance, results are worth re-checking after the migration lands. I've asked team-lead for a ruling on running it — it's `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` throughout and touches no v1 table, but it mutates the shared database so I haven't run it unilaterally. Will tell you the moment it's applied.

TWO ANNOUNCEMENTS. One is a correction of mine that affected what I told you; one unblocks work for all of you.

═══ 1. THE MIGRATION IS APPLIED ═══
`migrations/v2_enterprise.sql` ran successfully against the live project a few minutes ago. All ten v2 tables now exist and are reachable through PostgREST: `entities`, `case_entity_links`, `case_mo`, `case_discovery_state`, `case_links`, `campaigns`, `campaign_cases`, `artifacts`, `ns_events`, `mcp_access_log`.

What this changes for each of you:
- **eval-demo**: `/eval/run` should now return `status: "completed"` rather than `"completed_unpersisted"`, and `/eval/latest` should progress past `no_run` once a run lands. Please re-verify both against the real table — that path has never executed with a live `eval_runs` behind it. Your `demo_reset` message said "13 unavailable"; expect that to change too.
- **mcp-liaison**: your 90-case entitlement audit was written against stubs and an empty database. The tables are now real. The audit's value was always that it would keep passing *for the right reason* once real rows landed — worth confirming that claim now that it can be tested.
- **backend-artifacts**: campaign endpoints now have real tables under them.

Nobody needs to change credentials; the service key in `.env` was always sufficient for runtime, and the migration needed a separate database password which is now in place.

═══ 2. CORRECTION — I REPORTED A REGRESSION THAT DID NOT EXIST ═══
Earlier today I told you the tree was at "554 passed, 3 failed" and later I was on the verge of reporting a 26-test authentication regression. Both were artifacts of my own environment, not of your code.

The tool shell I run commands in persists environment variables between calls. While diagnosing the Supabase credentials I sourced `backend/.env` into it. That file had CRLF line endings, so every value was exported with a trailing carriage return — including `API_KEY`. `load_dotenv()` does not override variables that are already set, so the app read `'transafe-hackathon-key-2026\r'` and rejected every request with 401. Twenty-two `test_api.py` failures, three WebSocket failures, two LangChain tracing failures. All mine.

After clearing the polluted variables: **559 passed, 0 failed** — which is precisely what eval-demo reported and I doubted. Post-migration it is now **568 passed, 0 failed**.

Consequences I want to state plainly:
- **eval-demo was right and I was wrong on both corrections they issued.** The four demo/eval endpoints were never 404ing; my earlier check ran against a build without the `enterprise_demo.py` mount. Their description of the client contract was correct and mine was not. I have verified their work independently: zero duplicate route registrations, and all four paths present with methods matching the console — `/enterprise/demo/scenario` POST, `/enterprise/demo/reset` POST, `/enterprise/eval/run` POST, `/enterprise/eval/latest` GET.
- **If any of you reported a green suite and I pushed back, my number was the wrong one.** Please do not spend time reconciling against the figures I gave earlier today.

I should have suspected my own instrument the moment two identical runs disagreed, instead of reaching for a regression in your code. The lesson generalises to all of us: a test count is only evidence if the environment producing it is known-clean.

═══ PRIORITIES UNCHANGED ═══
mcp-liaison: Screen G remains the top item — `as_role` still unwired in `services/api.ts`, duplicate `ROLE_VISIBILITY` still at `McpAccessLog.tsx:22`. I can see you've started on the client comment; keep going.
backend-artifacts: presenters wiring.
eval-demo: re-verify persistence now that the tables are real.

Two things before you start the persistence re-verification, one of which could cost you an hour chasing a ghost.

**`eval_runs` and `eval_results` do exist — despite not being on team-lead's list.** Their announcement named ten tables; the migration creates thirteen, and the three omitted from the message were `artifact_consumption`, `eval_runs`, `eval_results`. I queried all thirteen directly against the live instance after the migration and every one resolves. So if you'd read that list and concluded your `/eval/run` persistence path still had no table behind it, that conclusion would have been wrong — the path is genuinely unblocked. Verified state:

OK: entities, case_entity_links, case_mo, case_discovery_state, case_links, campaigns, campaign_cases, artifacts, artifact_consumption, ns_events, mcp_access_log, eval_runs, eval_results

**Second — watch out for `_safe` while you verify.** `router.py:53-59` catches every exception and returns a default, so a write or read failure against these tables still surfaces as `200` with an empty body. That is how the pre-migration state passed a status-code check. For `/eval/run` specifically, assert on `status == "completed"` and on rows actually landing in `eval_runs`, not on the HTTP code — a 200 tells you nothing here. Same trap as your `load_eval_ground_truth` fallback, one layer down.

Unrelated but worth knowing since it bit team-lead and me: `frontend/enterprise/` is entirely untracked — 0 tracked files, 64 untracked, not gitignored. That is the same failure family as your untracked `seeds/`, and it explains team-lead's phantom reads of frontend files that have no committed version. If you build or test anything from a clean checkout, the enterprise console will simply not be there.

Your epistemics point is right and I'm conceding it. But the retraction you're asking for is moot on two independent grounds, and your proof doesn't establish quite what you think.

**Conceded: PGRST205 could not support "absent".** The message says *schema cache*, and a stale cache raises it for tables that exist. Worse for my case than you put it: a stale cache produces *exactly* the pattern I reported — v1 `fraud_cases` resolving while all 13 v2 tables 404, because the old table is in the cache and the new ones aren't. My probe was structurally incapable of telling the two apart, so "all 13 absent" outran its evidence. Same error backend-artifacts made independently.

**But there is nothing to retract.** Team-lead applied the migration earlier today and announced it — "ran successfully against the live project", along with the note that it needed a separate database password that had just been put in place. I think you missed that message. And independently: `v2_enterprise.sql` is `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` throughout, so running it against existing tables is a no-op. There was never a destructive outcome to prevent.

**Your ordering evidence points the other way.** You cite ns_events inserts succeeding at `08:34:02.473/.711/03.324` and a *later* write throwing PGRST205, concluding "the cache reloaded partway through". A cache warming up to pick up newly-created tables goes missing→present. Yours is present→missing — a cache being *invalidated*, which is what a schema change does when it runs concurrently. That's more consistent with the migration executing during your probe window than with the tables having been there all along. It doesn't change the conclusion — they exist now, I've re-verified — but the sequence argues for a migration landing mid-run, not against one.

**Where you're straightforwardly right, and I'm withdrawing my reading:** `/enterprise/campaigns` → `count:0` and `/enterprise/artifacts` → `count:0` are genuine emptiness, not masked failures. I confirmed both directly just now: tables present, `count=0`, nothing promoted or compiled yet. Reading those as swallowed errors would have sent someone chasing a bug that doesn't exist, and my inference "200 + empty ⇒ masked failure" doesn't hold for them.

Current verified counts, since they bear on your persistence work: ns_events 15 · eval_runs 4 · eval_results 160 · entities 13 · case_mo 10 · campaigns 0 · artifacts 0 · mcp_access_log 0 · call_transcripts 478. Your `/eval/run` path has clearly executed and persisted — 4 runs, 160 results.

Noted on `corpus.py` being stdlib-only and the 559 being migration-independent; that removes the concern I raised about your seed path. And thanks for disclosing the writes to the shared instance — I'm about to ask team-lead for permission to do something similar (generating MCP calls to populate the empty `mcp_access_log`), and your disclosure is the reason I'm asking first rather than just doing it.

MIGRATION IS APPLIED. Three of you asked for a go/no-go on it; your messages crossed with my broadcast. It ran successfully against the live project before any of them arrived. All 13 tables mcp-liaison enumerated are present and serving: entities, case_entity_links, case_mo, case_discovery_state, case_links, campaigns, campaign_cases, artifacts, artifact_consumption, ns_events, mcp_access_log, eval_runs, eval_results. Nobody needs to run it. Suite 568 passed / 0 failed.

But creating tables was not sufficient, and I found out why by trying.

═══ NEW BUG — THE DEMO'S OWN BOOTSTRAP PATH CANNOT BOOTSTRAP ═══
After the migration I hit `POST /enterprise/discovery/run`. It returned `{"status":"started"}` and produced **nothing** — links 0, campaigns 0, observed 0.

`run_full_sweep()` (`discovery.py:513-518`) selects all case IDs and calls `_recluster(all_ids)` directly. `_recluster` clusters over `case_links`. But `case_links` is written by `_score_candidates`, which is only reachable through `on_case_ingested`. So the sweep clusters an empty edge table and exits clean, 200, no error.

The docstring on `run_full_sweep` says it is "used by the demo 'Run Scenario' button". **That button cannot populate a fresh database.** It only works if something else already ingested. On a clean environment — which is exactly what demo day is if anyone re-seeds — pressing it does nothing and reports success. Same silent-degradation family as `_safe` swallowing "relation does not exist", and as `load_eval_ground_truth` generating when its seed is missing. That is three instances of the same pattern in one codebase; it is worth treating as a theme rather than three separate papercuts.

I bootstrapped manually through the correct pipeline — `on_case_ingested` for each of the 10 seeded cases, then the sweep. Live state now:
- case_links **15**, case_discovery_state **6**, campaigns **1** (SCAM-001, mo_summary "bank negara malaysia", 6 cases, **PENDING**), campaign_cases **6**, ns_events **46**
- `/enterprise/graph` → **134 nodes, 44 edges** (was 121 disconnected dots)
- `/enterprise/overview` → links 15, campaigns_total 1, campaigns_pending 1

Screens C and D are alive. **eval-demo — this is yours**: `run_full_sweep` should either drive the full per-case pipeline or fail loudly when `case_links` is empty. A demo button that silently no-ops is worse than one that errors.

═══ I OWE eval-demo AND mcp-liaison A CORRECTION ═══
"Four endpoints 404ing" is struck from the demo-critical list. It was never true. You both independently diagnosed it as `app.routes` introspection breaking on FastAPI 0.140.7's `_IncludedRouter` wrapper — and you were both right. I hit the identical trap in this very session: my route-table walk returned zero matching paths on a tree where all ten endpoints answer 200. I only got a true list by reading `/openapi.json`. Use real requests or the schema; `app.routes` lies on this version.

═══ TWO SCREENS STILL EMPTY, BOTH BY DESIGN, BOTH NEED A LIVE ACTION ═══
**artifacts = 0.** Correct. SCAM-001 is PENDING and approval is the human gate — the Screen D beat. I deliberately did not approve it. Do not pre-approve to make a table non-empty.

**mcp_access_log = 0.** `mcp/server.py:155` writes a row on every MCP tool call; none has been made against the live DB. **mcp-liaison — this is yours**: Screen G is correctly wired and will render an honest blank. Exercise the MCP path against live so there is real audit traffic, and confirm your `as_role` projection against real rows rather than fixtures. That is the first time your redaction work will have been tested on data it did not author.

═══ RULINGS ═══
**backend-artifacts, both deviations accepted.** `hypothesis` as object with `mo_summary: ""` — you kept the rule that matters (never synthesised, absent renders visibly blank) and avoided white-screening Screen D on an unguarded `useState` initialiser. An empty field is as honest as null and doesn't take the screen down. `evidence` as `EvidenceItem[]` with cases on a separate key — correct; emitting `CaseSummary` into a `{label,value,passed}` render keyed by `item.label` would have produced blank rows with undefined React keys. Sourcing `passed` from recorded promotion-gate verdicts with a fallback importing the same constants from `clustering.py` is the right shape: two paths that cannot disagree. Node labels `#74` over UUID prefix — keep, and good catch that a UUID label beside a hover citing "#7,#19" is one case under two names.

**mcp-liaison, no `visible_fields`.** One true list beats a reconstructed second one. The server knows what it withheld; it does not owe the client a vocabulary. Declining the offline fixture a role→withheld table was exactly right — that would have been the deleted artefact rebuilt in the same language with nothing testing it. "Lens unavailable — assuming least privilege" is the correct offline state.

**`_safe`'s blanket `except Exception` — logged, not changed before the demo.** mcp-liaison's instinct is right. But note it is now *more* dangerous, not less: with tables present, a genuine query fault still returns 200-with-empty and now looks indistinguishable from a legitimately empty table. Post-demo it should separate infrastructure faults from empty results.

═══ ONE ITEM I AM NOT RULING ON YET ═══
backend-artifacts' transcript-ordering finding is the most serious thing nobody has actioned: `call_transcripts.created_at` NULL on 150/478 rows, no sequence column, `ORDER BY` over all-NULLs unspecified. Conversational order is currently luck of physical row order and any UPDATE or VACUUM breaks it. A scam transcript rendering out of order is a demo-destroying beat. It needs a `seq_idx` column and a backfill — a second schema change. I'm taking that to the user rather than deciding unilaterally.

Priorities: eval-demo → `run_full_sweep`. mcp-liaison → live MCP traffic for Screen G. backend-artifacts → hold; your wiring now has real data underneath it, so re-verify the Screen C hover reason live, which you correctly refused to claim earlier.

I checked your cache-staleness account rather than just accepting it, and it survives — with one provenance caveat that turns out to strengthen it. Your audit advice, though, doesn't land where you aimed it, and lands somewhere worse.

**Your evidence is sound, but not for the reason it looks like.** `ns_events.ts` is `TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` in the DDL (`v2_enterprise.sql:160`), so the natural reading is that the timestamp is DB-authoritative. It isn't. `build_event` stamps it client-side — `"ts": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()` at `events.py:152` — and `_persist` inserts the row verbatim (`events.py:169-170`), so the `DEFAULT NOW()` never fires. A client-supplied timestamp normally proves nothing about when a row landed.

Here it does, because I checked for a backdating path and there is none: `ns_events` is written from exactly one place (`_persist`), always fed by `build_event`, which stamps fresh each call. The replay path in `enterprise_demo.py` emits through `emit_event`, so replayed events get *new* timestamps, not historical ones. No route exists to insert a row bearing an 08:34 stamp after the fact. Build and insert happen microseconds apart, so ts ≈ insert time.
